src.yaml.0-overview.name: Overview
src.yaml.0-overview.description: The shop in its world: who uses it and what it leans on. Open Shop to go inside; every diagram in the gallery is one side of it.

src.yaml.0-overview.1.name: One shop, seen from every side: open Shop for its parts, and a part for its own diagram. Every part is a usage of a definition in Parts or Records.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.name: Shop
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.description: The shop itself, one region a side: what customers reach, what runs behind it, and how it runs.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.ord.name: Orders
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.ord.description: Keeps every order and tells the rest of the shop when one is placed.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.pay.name: Payments
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.pay.description: Takes money for an order, once, and says whether it was taken. Open it for how a charge is retried.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.pay.name: A retried checkout repeats the same key, so a retry never charges twice.
Payment retry
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.back-office.pay.description: A flowchart, one of Payments' behaviours. It starts and ends at its marks; a decision's lines say where each answer goes.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.customer-facing.name: Storefront
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.customer-facing.description: An internal diagram: what the storefront is made of. Its pages meet through typed ports; its own ports sit on its walls.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.1-c.name: Checkout saga
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.1-c.description: A sequence: who talks to whom, in what order. Each lifeline is a reference to the part it stands for, so it is the same Gateway, Storefront and Payments the shop is made of.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.name: Fulfilment
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.description: A swimlane: who does what, in which phase. Each lane is a reference to the service that does the work.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.name: Pick items
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.body: Stock is taken off the shelf.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.name: Book carrier
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.2-f.body: Shipping books a pickup in the carrier's terms.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.3-d.name: Deployment
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.3-d.description: Where the shop runs. Groups nest, each a dashed box round its members with a note tied beside it; a grid lays environments under their headers.

src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.4-e.name: Estate
src.yaml.0-overview.shop.how-it-runs.4-e.description: A treemap: where the weight is. Each tile is as large as the service it stands for holds, gathered by the shop's regions.

src.yaml.Data.1-model.name: Model
src.yaml.Data.1-model.description: The records as classes — fields, then behaviours — joined by the associations stored between them, each end saying how many and in what role. Order status is a type, so it draws no card of its own.

src.yaml.Data.2-schema.name: Schema
src.yaml.Data.2-schema.description: The records as an entity relationship diagram — columns and keys — the same associations drawn as crow's feet.

src.yaml.Faces.1-small.1.name: Every card on its small face, the name and marks alone; the icon says what sort of thing it is.

src.yaml.Faces.2-large.1.name: Every large face. A layer whose cards are large draws what each says under its name.

src.yaml.Faces.2-large.4.name: Runbook
src.yaml.Faces.2-large.4.body:
# When orders stop flowing

Check the **relay** first. See the [outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

| signal | threshold | page |
|---|---|---|
| outbox rows | 10 000 | yes |
| relay lag | 60 s | no |

src.yaml.Faces.2-large.5.name: Charge once
src.yaml.Faces.2-large.5.body: Checkout retries the same request. The order service treats a repeated checkout key as the order it already created, so a retry never charges twice.

src.yaml.Faces.2-large.7.name: Release notes
src.yaml.Faces.2-large.7.body: v2 of the orders API: the checkout key is required.

src.yaml.Faces.2-large.8.name: Incident summary
src.yaml.Faces.2-large.8.body: Checkout was slow for twenty minutes while the card processor timed out. The breaker opened, the fallback queued charges, and every queued charge was taken once the processor came back.

src.yaml.Parts.actor.name: actor
src.yaml.Parts.actor.description: Someone outside the system who uses it. Drawn wherever they meet it.

src.yaml.Parts.external.name: external
src.yaml.Parts.external.description: A system nobody here runs. The shop meets it only at its edge.

src.yaml.Parts.page.name: page
src.yaml.Parts.page.description: A screen a customer uses. It shows something and asks for something, over HTTP.

src.yaml.Parts.service.name: service
src.yaml.Parts.service.description: Runs on its own, owns its data and speaks to others only through its ports. Every service names the team that runs it: check reports one that does not.

src.yaml.Parts.store.name: store
src.yaml.Parts.store.description: Keeps many records of one type, drawn as a table on its card. Records are values, never blocks.

src.yaml.Records.ledger.name: Ledger
src.yaml.Records.ledger.description: A store of orders: many records of one type, drawn as a table on its card.

src.yaml.Records.line.name: Line
src.yaml.Records.line.description: One product on an order, and how many.

src.yaml.Records.order.name: Order
src.yaml.Records.order.description: A customer's request, and the lines on it.

src.yaml.Records.order.1.name: place
src.yaml.Records.order.1.description: Takes a customer's lines and gives back the order they make.

src.yaml.Records.order.order-states.name: Order states
src.yaml.Records.order.order-states.description: A state machine, the Order record's lifecycle, ranked by where its transitions point. Each transition is named by the event that fires it.

src.yaml.Records.payment.name: Payment
src.yaml.Records.payment.description: A charge taken against an order.

src.yaml.Visuals.1-lines.1.name: Every relation the base ships, and the ways a line points. A line's ends say how many, in what role, and who owns whom.

src.yaml.Visuals.2-colour.1.name: Colour and line, set on a card. A family or a hue picks its colour; fill, border and opacity say how it is drawn.
